sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A function contains the points (1, 5) and (3, 13). Write the function rule f(x) = mx + b.

steps: Use one point to find b: 5 = 4(1) + b, so b = 1.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A rental company charges a $84 base fee plus $20 per hour. Which function models the total cost f(x) for x hours?
A hiker climbs a steady, unchanging slope for the whole hike. Which description best matches the shape of the graph over time?
choices: decreasing at a constant rate the whole time
increasing at a constant rate the whole time

items.prompt:
A graph shows height over time.
From t = 0 to t = 2, height goes from 0 to -8.
From t = 2 to t = 6, height goes from -8 to -8.
From t = 6 to t = 9, height goes from -8 to -7.
Which interval shows the height constant?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Consider the relation {(8, -10), (6, -15), (-4, -3), (-2, -11)}. Is this relation a function?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which set of ordered pairs does NOT represent a function?
